source.title: Keep the Gradients Flowing: Using Gradient Flow to Study Sparse Network Optimization
source.authors: Kale-ab Tessera; Sara Hooker; Benjamin Rosman

record.tranche_reason: The study compares test accuracy across optimizers and regularization settings, and measures a gradient-flow statistic; these are related measures, not direct tests of the listed claim versions’ core conditions.
record.gate_note: The study’s own results compare sparse and dense networks and report test accuracy and gradient flow. Figures 2–5 and 15–24 contain many results only as plots; rows below capture the textual comparisons the authors describe. Cited results from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4's decoupled-weight-decay qualification in sparse and dense image classifiers: its own AdamW-versus-Adam experiment reports better test performance with AdamW. The main sparse-versus-dense comparisons do not themselves establish an adaptive-versus-SGD generalization difference.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that sparse-network training requires attention beyond initialization: BatchNorm stabilizes gradient flow, Adam and RMSProp sometimes perform poorly with L2 or augmentation under high EGF, and Swish and PReLU are promising. They also report extensions to convolutional architectures and magnitude pruning.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines randomly sparse networks and matched-capacity dense networks, focusing on accuracy and gradient flow; it does not use the listed claim versions’ interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer, regularization or normalization configuration, learning rate, activation function, sparsity, and architecture type affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective Gradient Flow correlates with test accuracy and loss, with reported advantages over standard gradient norms in sparse networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-flow measures can predict sparse-network test performance; this is distinct from magnitude-aware sharpness tracking the generalization gap.

fits_no_version.finding: BatchNorm changes the relative performance of randomly sparse and matched-parameter dense networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The sparse-versus-dense accuracy advantage depends on normalization and optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Swish and PReLU improve performance in selected sparse-network configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-function choice affects sparse-network optimization and test accuracy.

record.problems: Many outcomes are shown only in figures; the paper’s main comparisons concern sparse versus matched-capacity dense networks, not the claim’s specified tests of generalization. Gradient flow is correlated with test performance, not the train–test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were retained: the paper’s plotted optimizer and regularization comparisons do not provide recoverable separate model-specific values for the adaptive-versus-SGD result relevant to V4. Other figure-only results are outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or natural-versus-random-label held-out comparison.
Widths vary, but the supplied text does not establish zero training error or test-error trends beyond the interpolation threshold.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or experiment learning local connectivity.

The supplied text does not establish condition-specific adaptive-versus-SGD accuracy rankings, equal or better training performance, recovery to SGD performance, broader tuning eliminating a gap, switching optimizers, or language-model results. Numerical optimizer comparisons are unavailable in the supplied figure text.
Dropout is proposed as future work, not tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or correlation with the train–test gap.
No removal of examples selected by label memorization.

missing.what: AdamW versus Adam with L2: better test performance and lower EGF in dense and sparse four-hidden-layer CIFAR-100 MLPs at learning rate 0.1. The text supplies a qualitative result even though numerical plot values are unavailable; rows_left_out does not specifically declare this comparison.

The Swish-plus-AdamW configuration achieves good CIFAR-100 Wide ResNet performance. Record the combined intervention explicitly; the prose does not isolate the contribution of decoupled weight decay or establish recovery to SGD.

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to fix. Wilcoxon tables compare sparse with dense networks within each optimizer; their p-values cannot establish optimizer rankings. The supplied text supports a qualitative AdamW verdict, but not numerical accuracy differences. Lower EGF is correlational evidence, not proof of a generalization mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.
No width sweep assessing test error beyond the width needed to fit the training set.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch.

The paper reports optimizer and regularization effects on sparse versus dense test accuracy, but its plotted outcomes do not give recoverable model-specific values for the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison. It does not test broader hyperparameter tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models.
The study correlates gradient-flow measures with test accuracy and loss, not magnitude-aware sharpness with the train–test gap.

relationships.condition: Dense and randomly sparse four-hidden-layer MLPs on CIFAR-100, learning rate 0.1: AdamW versus Adam with L2 regularization.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4.1.2 and Figure 23's caption, rather than extracted rows: decoupled weight decay improves test performance over Adam's L2 formulation. This supports the recovery mechanism, without demonstrating parity with SGD.
relationships.display_finding: The reported improvement from AdamW over Adam with L2 regularization remains unverified and does not establish parity with SGD.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
